System Requirements Document (SRD)
Version 2.0 — Enhanced Edition
Community Savings & Loan Manager (Njangi/Tontine Digitization Platform)
1. Introduction
1.1 Purpose

Mbole Pay is a web-based platform designed to digitize and automate community savings groups ("njangi" or "tontine") by leveraging smart contracts, automated payments, and transparent record-keeping. This document specifies the complete functional and non-functional requirements for the system, including dispute resolution rules, smart contract governance, compliance obligations, and data architecture.
1.2 Scope
Mbole Pay will:
Enable digital management of community savings groups
Automate transactions, contributions, and payouts using smart contracts on the Binance Smart Chain (BSC)
Provide secure and transparent financial tracking with dual storage (PostgreSQL + IPFS)
Support dispute resolution through anonymous, quorum-gated voting
Comply with COBAC/BEAC financial regulations and Cameroonian Law No. 2010/012 on cybersecurity
Offer an accessible, scalable, and secure platform for tontines across Cameroon and the CEMAC zone

1.4 Document Conventions
Requirements marked [NEW] were absent in v1 of this SRD and have been added in this revision. Requirements marked [UPDATED] have been materially revised from their original form.
2. Functional Requirements
2.1 User Management
2.1.1 User Registration & Authentication
Users can register via email, phone number, or social login (Google/Facebook OAuth2)
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) required for all accounts handling transactions above XAF 50,000
Admins can approve or reject member applications within 48 hours; pending members cannot contribute
Account suspension/reactivation by Super Admin, with mandatory reason logging
Password recovery via OTP to registered phone number or email
2.1.2 KYC / Identity Verification [NEW]
All users must complete tiered KYC verification before initiating or receiving payments:
KYC Tier
Requirements & Transaction Limits
Tier 0 — Basic
Phone number verified. Limit: XAF 50,000 per transaction, XAF 200,000 per month
Tier 1 — Standard
National ID (CNI) uploaded and verified. Limit: XAF 500,000 per transaction, XAF 2,000,000 per month
Tier 2 — Full
ID + proof of address + selfie liveness check. No per-transaction limit; AML monitoring applies above XAF 5,000,000

KYC verification should integrate with a regional identity provider (e.g., MTN Identity or a COBAC-approved bureau). Documents are stored encrypted in IPFS; only the verification status is held in PostgreSQL.
2.1.3 Role-Based Access Control
Contribute, view own transactions, vote on disputes, download personal statements:
Members
Create groups, manage members, set payout rules, view group-level reports:
Admins
Platform-wide management, compliance reports, audit log access, freeze/unfreeze groups:
Super Admins
2.2 Savings Group Management
2.2.1 Group Creation & Configuration
Admins create groups with configurable rules: contribution amount, frequency (weekly/biweekly/monthly), payout order method (first-come or lottery), and minimum member count
Group rules are immutable once the first contribution cycle begins; rule changes require a new group or unanimous member vote
Each group is associated with a dedicated smart contract instance deployed at creation
2.2.2 Member Lifecycle
Members join a group by invitation or application; Admin approval required
Waiting list supported: members who apply after a cycle begins are queued for the next cycle
2.2.3 Member Exit Rules [NEW]
The following rules govern member departure mid-cycle:
A member may request to exit before their scheduled payout date
Exit request is subject to Admin approval and a 7-day notice period
If the member has already received their payout: they must repay the outstanding contribution balance before exit is confirmed

If the member has not yet received their payout: their payout entitlement is forfeited unless the group votes (simple majority) to return their contributions minus a penalty fee (default: 5%, configurable per group)
The vacated payout slot is moved to the end of the queue or redistributed by lottery, per group rules
All exit events are recorded on-chain as immutable audit entries
2.2.4 Group Dissolution [NEW]
Groups may be dissolved under the following conditions:
Unanimous member vote to dissolve
All scheduled payout cycles are complete (natural dissolution)
Super Admin intervention due to regulatory non-compliance or fraud determination
Dissolution procedure:
All outstanding payouts are triggered immediately by the smart contract
Undistributed funds (e.g., penalty reserves) are distributed proportionally to all members
The group's smart contract is marked inactive (not destructed, to preserve audit trail)
A final dissolution report is generated and stored on IPFS, linked to the group record in PostgreSQL
The Admin holding dissolution authority must be Tier 2 KYC verified
2.3 Payment & Payout Processing
2.3.1 Contribution Collection
Supports mobile money (MTN MoMo, Orange Money), bank transfer, and card payments via Flutterwave/Paystack
Auto-debit for scheduled contributions triggered by the smart contract payout scheduler
Contribution confirmation is only recorded on-chain after payment gateway webhook confirms settlement
2.3.2 Payout Scheduling
First-come, first-paid system based on agreed payout sequence encoded in the smart contract at group creation
Automated notifications to recipients 48 hours and 24 hours before payout execution
Payouts execute automatically when all members in the current cycle have contributed
2.3.3 Payment Failure Handling [NEW]
The system must handle payment and payout failures gracefully. The following retry and escalation logic applies:
Failure Scenario
System Response
Auto-debit fails (member)
Retry after 24 h. After 3 failed retries: mark member delinquent, notify Admin, pause member's payout eligibility
Payout transfer fails (gateway timeout)
Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1h, 4h, 12h). If all fail: hold funds in escrow smart contract, alert Admin and Recipient
Payout fails (recipient account invalid)
Admin notified. Member must update payment details within 72 h or payout is deferred to next cycle and their queue position moves to end
Gateway API down > 15 min
Queue payout via Redis message queue; process automatically when gateway recovers. SLA: max 4-hour delay
Smart contract execution error
Transaction reverted; funds not moved. Admin and Super Admin alerted. Manual intervention required; logged in audit trail
All deferred or failed payouts must appear prominently on the group Admin dashboard with status, retry count, and escalation timestamp.
2.4 Dispute Resolution
2.4.1 Raising a Dispute
Any member may raise a dispute against a contribution record, a payout execution, or a member's conduct
Disputes must include: category (payment/conduct/rule), description (max 1,000 chars), and optional evidence attachment (stored on IPFS)
A member may not raise more than 3 active disputes simultaneously
2.4.2 Voting Rules [NEW]
All dispute votes are anonymous. The following rules govern the process:
Parameter
Rule
Voting window
72 hours from dispute submission (configurable per group: 48–96 h)
Quorum
Minimum 60% of active group members must vote for the result to be binding
Resolution threshold
Simple majority (>50%) of cast votes determines the outcome
Tie-break
If votes are exactly split (50/50), the dispute is escalated to the group Admin for casting decision. Admin decision is final and logged on-chain.
Admin-conflict rule
If the dispute implicates the group Admin, they are automatically recused. Super Admin assumes the tie-break role for that dispute.
Quorum not reached
If quorum is not reached within the voting window, the dispute is auto-escalated to Super Admin for review within 48 hours
Repeat disputes
A member may not re-raise a dispute on the same event within 30 days of a resolved vote
2.4.3 Dispute Execution
Majority-approved resolutions are executed by the smart contract (e.g., reversal of contribution record, member penalty)
All votes, outcomes, and smart contract executions are recorded on-chain as an immutable audit trail
Parties to the dispute receive SMS/email notification of outcome within 1 hour of resolution
2.5 Reporting & Notifications
Downloadable member statements (PDF) covering contributions, payouts, and dispute history
Group dashboards with: total pool size, contribution compliance rate, pending payouts, active disputes
Real-time SMS/email alerts for: contribution received, payout scheduled, payout sent, dispute raised, dispute resolved, delinquency warning
Notification channels configurable per user (SMS only, email only, or both)
Report export formats: PDF and CSV
3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Performance
System handles 10,000+ concurrent users under normal load
REST API response time: under 500ms at P95 for read operations, under 1,500ms for write operations
End-to-end transaction confirmation (payment gateway + on-chain): under 3 seconds for BSC transactions at standard gas
Notification delivery: SMS within 60 seconds, email within 120 seconds of triggering event
[NEW] Load-testing baseline: 10,000 concurrent users simulated using k6 or Locust before each major release. Results documented in CI/CD pipeline artifacts.
3.2 Security
End-to-end encryption (TLS 1.3) for all API traffic
AES-256 encryption at rest for all user PII and financial data in PostgreSQL
Smart contract audits by an independent security firm before mainnet deployment and after any contract upgrade
Secure authentication via OAuth2 + JWT sessions (access token TTL: 15 minutes; refresh token TTL: 7 days)
All admin actions logged in a tamper-evident audit log (append-only, IPFS-anchored)

[NEW] Security testing cadence: annual external penetration test + continuous SAST via GitHub Actions (Semgrep/Snyk). Critical findings block deployment. Smart contract audit required before BSC mainnet go-live and after any Solidity code change.
3.3 Scalability
Infrastructure as Code (Terraform + Ansible) for automated environment provisioning
Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaling: Backend API scales from 2 to 20 pods based on CPU/memory thresholds
Database read replicas for reporting queries; primary PostgreSQL instance for writes
BSC throughput ceiling: ~100 TPS; groups with >500 members or >100 simultaneous payouts should use batched contract calls to stay within this limit

[NEW] Database sharding strategy: partition contribution and payout tables by group_id. Groups exceeding 10,000 transactions are migrated to a dedicated shard. IPFS cluster with pinning service (Pinata or Web3.Storage) for high-availability document storage.
3.4 Usability
Mobile-first responsive design (breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px)
Multilingual support: English, French, Cameroonian Pidgin (default: French)
WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance for all public-facing pages
Offline-capable progressive web app (PWA) for core read operations (contribution history, group status)
[NEW] Accessibility requirement: WCAG 2.1 AA minimum. Screen reader support required for all form flows. Contrast ratio ≥4.5:1 on all text. Keyboard navigation for all interactive elements.
3.5 Compliance [UPDATED]
Mbole Pay operates primarily in Cameroon and the CEMAC economic zone. The following regulatory frameworks apply:
3.5.1 Primary Regulatory Framework (CEMAC Zone)

All payment processing activities involving third-party funds must comply with COBAC Regulation R-2009/02 on electronic money. Mbole Pay must obtain or partner with a COBAC-licensed electronic money institution before processing live transactions.:
COBAC (Commission Bancaire de l’Afrique Centrale)
Cross-border fund transfers within the CEMAC zone comply with BEAC foreign exchange rules. International transfers (outside CEMAC) require additional clearance.:
BEAC Regulations

Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing obligations per CEMAC Directive No. 01/11-CEMAC-UMAC-CM. Suspicious transaction reporting (STR) to GABAC required for transactions matching risk thresholds (see KYC tiers above).:
CEMAC AML/CFT Directive

On cybersecurity and cybercrime. User personal data processed by Mbole Pay is subject to this law. Data storage on servers physically located in Cameroon or a CEMAC country is preferred; if AWS/GCP/Azure regions outside CEMAC are used, data transfer agreements and encryption-at-rest are mandatory.:
Cameroonian Law No. 2010/012
3.5.2 Secondary / International Compliance

Applies only to users who are EU residents. EU-resident user data must be handled under a lawful basis (consent or legitimate interest) with data subject rights (access, erasure, portability) implemented.:
GDPR
Card payment handling must comply with PCI-DSS Level 4 standards. Card data must NOT be stored by Mbole Pay; all card tokenization is delegated to Flutterwave/Paystack.:
PCI-DSS
3.5.3 Smart Contract Governance
Smart contract code published to a public repository before deployment (open-source audit)
No single admin wallet may hold exclusive control over contract upgrade keys; multi-sig (3-of-5) required for all privileged contract operations
Contract upgrade events emit on-chain events visible to all members
4. System Architecture
4.1 High-Level Architecture
Layer
Technology & Rationale
Frontend
React.js + TailwindCSS. Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline support for low-connectivity environments.
Backend API
Node.js + Express.js. REST endpoints. Stateless, horizontally scalable. JWT authentication.
Auth Service
Decoupled JWT/OAuth2 service. Allows all microservices to verify tokens independently.
API Gateway
TLS termination, rate limiting (100 req/min per IP), request routing, DDoS protection.
Message Queue
Redis Streams for async payout scheduling, notification dispatch, and payment retry logic.
Primary Database
PostgreSQL 15. Handles all transactional data (users, groups, contributions, payouts, disputes). Row-level security for multi-tenancy.
Immutable Storage
IPFS (via Pinata pinning service). Stores KYC documents, dispute evidence, audit trail entries, and dissolution reports. Content-addressed — tamper-evident by design.
Blockchain
Binance Smart Chain (BSC) mainnet. Smart contracts in Solidity, compiled and tested via Hardhat. Web3.js for backend-to-chain communication.
Infrastructure
Docker containers, Kubernetes (K8s) orchestration, Terraform IaC, GitHub Actions CI/CD, hosted on AWS/GCP (CEMAC-region preferred).
4.2 Blockchain Selection Rationale [NEW]
Ethereum mainnet was evaluated and rejected for the following reasons:

Gas fees on Ethereum mainnet average $2–$15 per transaction. A tontine group of 20 members making monthly contributions would incur $480–$3,600/year in gas alone — prohibitive for the target demographic.
Binance Smart Chain (BSC) is selected as the primary deployment chain for the following reasons:
Factor
BSC Position
Average gas fee
~$0.01–0.10 per transaction. Viable at target transaction volumes.
Transaction throughput
~100 TPS; sufficient for expected load (see scalability limits above)
EVM compatibility
Full Solidity + Hardhat + Web3.js support. Minimal re-work from Ethereum toolchain.
Ecosystem
MTN MoMo and Flutterwave have existing BSC integrations; reduces bridge complexity.
Risk
BSC is more centralized than Ethereum; noted as acceptable trade-off for cost at this stage

Polygon (PoS) is the recommended migration path if BSC throughput or centralization becomes a concern at scale. The contract architecture should use an upgradeable proxy pattern (OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy) to enable chain migration without data loss.
4.3 Data Storage Architecture [NEW]
The following table defines what data lives in each storage layer and why:
Data Type
Storage Layer & Justification
User profiles, KYC status, group config, contribution records, payout schedule
PostgreSQL — requires ACID transactions, relational queries, and fast reads
JWT sessions, payout job queues, notification queues, rate-limit counters
Redis — ephemeral, high-speed key-value access
KYC documents (ID scans, selfies), dispute evidence attachments
IPFS (Pinata pinned) — immutable, content-addressed; only the IPFS CID (hash) is stored in PostgreSQL
Audit trail entries (admin actions, dissolution events, dispute outcomes)
IPFS — tamper-evident; CID stored in PostgreSQL and anchored on-chain in smart contract event logs
Smart contract state (payout queue, contribution balances, dispute votes)
BSC (on-chain) — authoritative source of truth for financial state; PostgreSQL mirrors it for fast querying
Financial transaction receipts, member statements
PostgreSQL (generated) + IPFS (archived PDF) — queryable in DB, long-term tamper-proof copy on IPFS

Consistency rule: when a smart contract event is emitted on-chain, the Backend API must update the PostgreSQL mirror within 30 seconds via event listener. Any query returning financial state must cross-check against on-chain state for amounts above XAF 100,000.
4.4 Smart Contract Architecture [NEW]
4.4.1 Contract Structure
One MbolePay factory contract manages group creation and platform-level config
Each savings group has its own MbolePayGroup contract instance deployed by the factory
All contracts use OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern to enable bug fixes without data loss
Admin keys use a Gnosis Safe multi-sig wallet (3-of-5 signers) for all privileged operations
4.4.2 Core Contract Functions
Function
Description
createGroup()
Deploys a new MbolePayGroup proxy; records group rules on-chain; emits GroupCreated event
recordContribution(address, uint256)
Records a member contribution; updates running total; checks if payout threshold is met
schedulePayout(address)
Adds address to payout queue; emits PayoutQueued event; called by recordContribution when cycle is complete
executePayout(address, uint256)
Transfers funds to recipient via payment gateway bridge; emits PayoutExecuted event; updates queue
raiseDispute(bytes32, string)
Opens a dispute record; emits DisputeRaised event; starts voting window timer
castVote(bytes32, bool)
Anonymous vote via commit-reveal scheme; emits VoteCast event (no voter identity exposed)
resolveDispute(bytes32)
Callable after voting window closes; tallies votes; executes resolution if quorum met; emits DisputeResolved
pauseGroup()
Emergency pause; stops all contributions and payouts; requires 3-of-5 multi-sig
upgradeContract(address)
Upgrades proxy implementation; requires 3-of-5 multi-sig + 48-hour timelock; emits Upgraded event
4.4.3 Failure & Recovery
All payable functions use Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern to prevent re-entrancy attacks
Failed payout executions revert cleanly; funds remain in contract escrow until resolved
Contract pause function (multi-sig gated) allows emergency halt without contract destruction
Upgrade timelock (48 hours) ensures members have visibility of any contract changes before they take effect
5. Constraints & Assumptions
5.1 Constraints
BSC gas fees must be budgeted into group operating costs; recommended: platform charges a 0.5% service fee per payout to cover gas costs
Mobile money integration depends on MTN MoMo and Orange Money API availability in Cameroon; fallback to Flutterwave card processing required
COBAC licensing must be obtained or a licensed partner engaged before handling real-money transactions
Smart contract upgrades require a 48-hour timelock and multi-sig; emergency patches cannot be deployed in under 48 hours
5.2 Assumptions
Users have access to a smartphone with internet connectivity (2G minimum for PWA offline mode)
Tontine groups are willing to adopt digital solutions and undergo KYC verification
MTN MoMo is the primary payment rail for Cameroonian users (>65% market share)
BSC gas fees remain below $0.50 per transaction on average; if fees exceed this threshold, migration to Polygon PoS is triggered
6. Future Enhancements
AI-based fraud detection for abnormal contribution/payout patterns
Decentralized Identity (DID) integration for enhanced member verification without centralized KYC storage
Integration with local microfinance institutions for credit scoring based on tontine history
Layer-2 migration to Polygon PoS if BSC costs or centralization risk exceeds acceptable thresholds
Multi-chain support enabling group members to contribute from different chains via a bridge
7. Glossary [NEW]
The following terms are used throughout this document with specific meaning:
Term
Definition
Tontine

A rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA) where a group of individuals each contribute a fixed amount periodically. The total pool is distributed to one member per cycle, rotating until all members have received it once.
Njangi
The Cameroonian/Central African name for a tontine. Used interchangeably in this document.
Cycle
One complete round of contributions in which every active member has contributed once and the pool has been paid out to the designated recipient.
Payout Queue
The ordered list of members who will receive the pooled contribution amount, one per cycle. Order is set at group creation and is immutable unless a member exits or a dispute alters it.
Quorum
The minimum percentage of eligible voters who must participate in a dispute vote for the outcome to be binding. Set at 60% by default.
COBAC
Commission Bancaire de l’Afrique Centrale — the banking regulator for the CEMAC economic zone, which includes Cameroon.
BEAC
Banque des États de l’Afrique Centrale — the central bank of the CEMAC zone; governs monetary policy and foreign exchange.
CEMAC
Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l’Afrique Centrale — the economic and monetary community of Central Africa (Cameroon, CAR, Congo, Gabon, Chad, Equatorial Guinea).
GABAC
Groupe d’Action contre le Blanchiment d’Argent en Afrique Centrale — the CEMAC financial intelligence unit. Mbole Pay must file STRs with GABAC when required.
AML/CFT
Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Terrorism Financing. A set of regulatory obligations to detect and report suspicious financial activity.
STR
Suspicious Transaction Report — a mandatory report filed with GABAC when a transaction meets risk criteria defined in CEMAC Directive No. 01/11.
KYC
Know Your Customer — the process of verifying the identity of users before allowing financial transactions.
BSC
Binance Smart Chain — an EVM-compatible blockchain with low transaction fees, selected as the deployment chain for Mbole Pay smart contracts.
Gas Fee
The cost paid to BSC validators to execute a smart contract transaction. Denominated in BNB.
IPFS
InterPlanetary File System — a distributed, content-addressed file storage protocol. Files are immutable once stored; the CID (content hash) acts as a permanent, tamper-evident reference.
CID
Content Identifier — the unique hash produced by IPFS for any stored file. Serves as the address and integrity proof of that file.
Multi-sig
Multi-signature wallet — a smart contract wallet requiring M-of-N key holders to approve a transaction before it executes. Used for all privileged contract operations.
Proxy Contract
An upgradeable smart contract pattern (OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy) where logic can be replaced without losing stored data.
Timelock
A mandatory delay (48 hours for Mbole Pay) between a contract upgrade being proposed and it taking effect, giving members visibility before changes are enacted.
WCAG 2.1 AA
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.1, Level AA — the international standard for web accessibility. Required for all Mbole Pay public-facing pages.
PWA
Progressive Web App — a web application that can be installed on a device and provides offline functionality, used here for low-connectivity resilience.
